source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ οἱ πονεῖν ἕτοιμοι ἐπὶ τοῖς καλλίστοις οὐ πρότερον ἀποστήσονται ζητοῦντες τὴν ἀλήθειαν πρὶν ἂν τὴν ἀπόδειξιν ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν λάβωσι τῶν γραφῶν. ἔστι μὲν οὖν κοινά τινα τῶν ἀνθρώπων κριτήρια καθάπερ τὰ αἰσθητήρια. τὰ δ᾿ ἄλλα τῶν βουληθέντων καὶ ἀσκησάντων τὰ ἀληθῆ. τὰ διὰ νοῦ καὶ λογισμοῦ τεχνικὰ λόγων ἀληθῶν τε καὶ ψευδῶν. μέγιστον δὲ τὸ καὶ τὴν οἴησιν ἀποθέσθαι. ἐν μέσῳ καταστάντας ἀκριβοῦς ἐπιστήμης καὶ προπετοῦς δοξοσοφίας, καὶ γνῶναι ὅτι ὁ τὴν αἰώνιον ἐλπίζων ἀνάπαυσιν γιγνώσκει καὶ τὴν εἴσοδον αὐτῆς ἐπίπονον οὖσαν καὶ »τεθλιμμένην«. ὁ δὲ ἅπαξ εὐαγγελισθεὶς καὶ »τὸ σωτήριόν« φησιν »ἰδών«, ἐν ᾗ ὥρᾳ ἂν ἐπιγνῷ, μὴ »ἐπιστρεφέσθω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καθάπερ ἡ Αὼτ γυνὴ« μηδὲ εἰς τὸν πρότερον βίον τὸν τοῖς αἰσθητοῖς προσανέχοντα, μηδὲ μὴν εἰς τὰς αἱρέσεις παλινδρομείτω· ἐρίζουσι γὰρ ἁμῇ γέ πῃ, τὸν ὄντα μὴ γινώσκουσαι θεόν. »ὁ γὰρ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμέ«, τὸν ὄντως πατέρα καὶ διδάσκαλον τῆς ἀληθείας, τὸν ἀναγεννῶντα καὶ ἀνακτίζοντα καὶ τιθηνούμενον τὴν ψυχὴν τὴν ἐξειλεγμένην, »οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος«, ἄξιος λέγει τοῦ εἶναι υἱὸς θεοῦ καὶ μαθητὴς θεοῦ ὁμοῦ καὶ φίλος καὶ συγγενής. »οὐδεὶς γὰρ εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω βλέπων καὶ ἐπιβάλλων τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐπ᾿ ἄροτρον εὔθετος τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.« Ἀλλ᾿. ὡς ἔοικεν. τοῖς πολλοῖς καὶ μέχρι νῦν δοκεῖ ἡ Μαριὰμ λεχὼ εἶναι διὰ τὴν τοῦ παιδίου γέννησιν, οὐκ οὖσα λεχώ (καὶ γὰρ μετὰ τὸ τεκεῖν αὐτὴν μαιωθεῖσάν φασί τινες παρθένον εὑρεθῆναι)· τοιαῦται δ᾿ ἡμῖν αἱ κυριακαὶ γραφαί, τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἀποτίκτουσαι καὶ μένουσαι παρθένοι μετὰ τῆς ἐπικρύψεως τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας μυστηρίων. »τέτοκεν καὶ οὐ τέτοκεν«, φησὶν ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἂν ἐξ αὑτῆς. οὐκ ἐκ συνδυασμοῦ συλλαβοῦσα. διόπερ τοῖς γνωστικοῖς κεκυήκασιν αἱ γραφαί, αἱ δὲ αἱρέσεις οὐκ ἐκμαθοῦσαι ὡς μὴ κεκυηκυίας παραπέμπονται. πάντων δὲ ἀνθρώπων τὴν αὐτὴν κρίσιν ἐχόντων οἱ μὲν ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ αἱροῦντι λόγῳ ποιοῦνται τὰς πίστεις, οἱ δὲ ἡδοναῖς σφᾶς αὐτοὺς ἐκδεδωκότες βιάζονται πρὸς τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τὴν γραφήν. δεῖ δ᾿, οἶμαι, τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐραστῇ ψυχικῆς εὐτονίας· σφάλλεσθαι γὰρ ἀνάγκη μέγιστα τοὺς μεγίστοις ἐγχειροῦντας πράγμασιν, ἢν μὴ τὸν κανόνα τῆς ἀληθείας παρ᾿ αὐτῆς λαβόντες ἔχωσι τῆς ἀληθείας. οἱ τοιοῦτοι δέ, ἅτε ἀποπεσόντες τῆς ὀρθῆς ὁδοῦ. κἀν τοῖς πλείστοις τῶν κατὰ μέρος σφάλλονται εἰκότως. διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ἀληθῶν καὶ ψευδῶν κριτήριον συγγεγυμνασμένον ἀκριβῶς τὰ δέοντα αἱρεῖσθαι. εἰ γὰρ ἐκέκτηντο, ταῖς θείαις ἐπείθοντο ἂν γραφαῖς.
pass_a_gloss: But those ready to labor for the best things will not stop seeking the truth before they receive the proof from the scriptures. There are indeed some common criteria of men, like the senses. But for those who have willed and practiced the true things, there are technical words of truth and falsehood through mind and reasoning. The greatest thing is to put away opinion. Having stood in the middle of exact knowledge and forward doctrine, and knowing that the one hoping for eternal rest also knows the entrance to it is laborious and 'afflicted'. But the one who has once been evangelized and says 'I have seen the salvation', in whatever hour he recognizes, let him not turn back to the things behind like the woman Lot, nor to the former life which yields to the senses, nor let him waver to the heresies; for they contend in a similar way, not knowing the existing God. 'For the one loving father or mother more than me', the truly father and teacher of truth, the one regenerating and redeeming and nourishing the chosen soul, 'is not worthy of me', he says, worthy of being son of God and disciple of God, and friend and relative. 'For no one looking back and putting his hand on the plow is fit for the kingdom of God.' But, as it seems, to many even now the Mary who gave birth appears to be a woman who has given birth because of the birth of the child, not being a woman who has given birth (for some say that after she gave birth, she was found a virgin); such are the lordly scriptures to us, giving birth to the truth and remaining virgins after the covering of the mysteries of truth. 'She has given birth and has not given birth', the scripture says, as if from itself, not having conceived from a union. Therefore, the scriptures have been impregnated with the truth for the knowledgeable, but the heresies, not having learned as if not having been impregnated, are sent away. All men having the same judgment, some follow the choosing word and make their beliefs, but others, having given themselves over to pleasures, force the scripture to their desires. It is necessary, I think, for the lover of truth to have psychic strength; for it is necessary for those attempting the greatest matters to fail greatly, unless they have the standard of truth, having taken it from truth itself. Such people, having fallen away from the straight path, fail in most of the partial things, reasonably, because they do not have a criterion of true and false things, trained to choose exactly what is necessary. For if they had it, they would obey the divine scriptures.

bible_refs.note: loving father or mother more than me

pass_b_english: Those who are ready to labor for the highest good will not cease seeking the truth until they receive its proof from the Scriptures. Indeed, there are certain criteria common to all people, like the senses. But for those who have chosen and practiced the true things, there are technical terms for truth and falsehood that operate through mind and reasoning. The greatest task is to set aside mere opinion. One must stand between exact knowledge and reckless pretension to wisdom, recognizing that the one who hopes for eternal rest also knows that the entrance to it is laborious and "afflicted." But the one who has once been evangelized and declares, "I have seen the salvation," must not, in whatever hour he recognizes it, turn back to the things behind like Lot's wife, nor return to the former life that attends to the senses, nor waver toward heresies; for these contend in a similar way, not knowing the true God. "For the one loving father or mother more than me" (Matt 10:37) — the true Father and teacher of truth, the one regenerating, rebuilding, and nurturing the chosen soul — "is not worthy of me." He says such a person is worthy of being a son of God and a disciple of God together, both a friend and a relative. "For no one looking back and putting his hand to the plow is fit for the kingdom of God" (Luke 9:62). Yet, as it seems, to many even now Mary appears to be a woman who has given birth because of the child's birth, though she is not a woman who has given birth in the ordinary sense (for some say that after she gave birth, she was found to be a virgin still). Such are the lordly Scriptures to us: they give birth to the truth and remain virgins after the veiling of the mysteries of truth. "She has given birth and has not given birth," says the Scripture, as if from itself, not having conceived from a union. Therefore the Scriptures have been impregnated with the truth for the knowledgeable, but the heresies, not having learned as if not impregnated, are sent away. All people possess the same capacity for judgment: some follow the choosing Word and form their beliefs accordingly, while others, having surrendered themselves to pleasures, force Scripture to conform to their desires. It is necessary, I think, for the lover of truth to possess psychic strength; for those who attempt the greatest matters are bound to fail greatly unless they hold the standard of truth, having received it from truth itself. Such people, having fallen from the straight path, naturally fail in most particular matters because they lack a criterion of true and false things that has been rigorously trained to choose exactly what is needed. For if they possessed it, they would obey the divine Scriptures.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the third-person imperative (ἐπιστρεφέσθω) and the specific theological metaphors regarding the Virgin Mary and the 'impregnated' scriptures. Scripture citations (Matt 10:37 and Luke 9:62) are correctly identified and added to Pass B as required. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
